decisions.rationale: Lead Farigiraf + Heliolisk: Armor Tail protects the eventual Trick Room mode from Weavile/Scizor priority while Heliolisk immediately pressures Charizard and Rotom-W. Camerupt and Mawile capitalize on Trick Room and punish the known Steel-heavy four.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill leads to threaten their Fire/Ground core with Mold Breaker Earthquake and eliminate Farigiraf pre-Trick Room. reflections.summary: Won by establishing Trick Room with Farigiraf while Armor Tail denied Scizor’s Bullet Punch, then using Helping Hand support to convert Heliolisk into a clean Charizard-Y endgame answer. The four brought fit the matchup; Mega Camerupt was useful but its immediate Earthquake trade into sash Excadrill was risky.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the Farigiraf/Heliolisk/Camerupt/Mawile four, but protect Mega Camerupt rather than exposing it to an unchecked Excadrill Earthquake when it first enters; preserve it for Trick Room pressure after Excadrill is weakened or removed.
reflections.notebook: Opponent uses Charizard-Y sun with Focus Sash Mold Breaker Excadrill and Technician Scizor; Mamoswine has Focus Band. Armor Tail reliably denies their revealed priority Bullet Punch and Ice Shard. Farigiraf Trick Room plus Helping Hand Heliolisk is a strong Charizard-Y endgame plan. Respect Excadrill Earthquake when bringing Mega Camerupt in; avoid relying on immediate spread-KO damage through sash/band survival effects.

reflections.summary: Lost because the opponent's Trick Room strategy completely neutralized our sun-speed sweep gameplan. Farigiraf set Trick Room on Turn 1 and maintained it for 5 turns, flipping speed tiers so our fast Pokemon (Charizard-Mega-Y at 167 Spe, Excadrill at 154 Spe) moved last. Farigiraf's Armor Tail shut down Scizor's Bullet Punch twice, while Helping Hand boosted Heliolisk's Thunderbolt into a one-turn kill on Mega Charizard-Y at 21% HP. Our team had zero tools against Trick Room—no setter, no Taunt, and no way to threaten Farigiraf through Protect stalling. The team preview plan of four sun-speed sweepers with no Trick Room answer was the root issue.
reflections.adjustment: Replace one team slot (Mamoswine contributed little—died to spread on Turn 3 without meaningful impact) with either a Trick Room setter to fight speed wars on our terms, or a Taunt user that can prevent Farigiraf from setting Trick Room and stall-busting through Protect. Alternatively, bring a fast special attacker capable of OHKOing Farigiraf before it clicks Trick Room on Turn 1.
reflections.notebook: Opponent runs Trick Room sun archetype: Farigiraf (Armor Tail / Helping Hand / Mental Herb) is the linchpin—sets Trick Room, blocks contact priority with Armor Tail, and sustains partner with Helping Hand. Heliolisk (Solar Power / Timid) under Trick Room uses Thunderbolt as a nuke; Solar Power chip damage is minor—still fires a lethal Thunderbolt in sun. Camerupt-Mega is a mid-game wallbreaker with spread Heat Wave; Mawile (Intimidate) punishes physical attackers on switch-in. Floette-Eternal and Tauros-Paldea-Combat were held in reserve—expect potential pivots in Game 3. Key lesson: sun speed-sweep cores need at least one Trick Room deterrent (Taunt, setter, or fast neutral hit). Farigiraf's bulk lets it survive unboosted hits and keep setting up; must threaten it on preview or have an answer to Trick Room itself.
